materials and methods: this cross-sectional study investigated the relationship between prenatal marijuana exposure and neuroimaging markers of brain health. data was obtained from the adolescent brain cognitive development study, a large, demographically diverse, multicenter cohort. the study included 1,085 children, 418 of whom were prenatally exposed to marijuana and 667 matched controls parahippocampal and right hemisphere postcentral gyrus. conclusions: overall, our findings suggest that prenatal exposure to marijuana may have long lasting alterations in children brain
